verdicts.summary: Web and server paths hold: old servers are gated off (ProviderModelPicker.tsx:140, ServerEnvironment.ts:252), the singleFlight key separates modelCatalogOnly (client-runtime/src/state/server.ts:1444), and recoverRefreshFailure swallows failures. The break is on mobile: the capability check runs once on mount with no retry.
verdicts.consequence: On mobile, if the environment's server config is not yet in environmentServerConfigsAtom when ThreadSettingsMainContent mounts, the refresh is silently skipped for that mount and the model list stays as it was. No error is shown.
verdicts.scenario: 1) The thread-settings main page mounts while registry.get(environmentServerConfigsAtom).get(environmentId) is undefined (line 921). 2) Line 922 returns early because config?.environment.capabilities.modelCatalogRefresh is not true. 3) The effect at lines 926-928 has deps [], so it never re-runs while that page stays mounted. 4) No modelCatalogOnly RPC is sent for that open. The web picker is not affected: it re-runs on each open via [isMenuOpen] (ProviderModelPicker.tsx:416-418 in the diff).

verdicts.summary: The recorded updatedAt is never ahead of what probes read. refreshAll reads the manifest at pass start (ProviderRegistry.ts:655-656), probes read the catalog later (CodexDriver.ts:236-238, ClaudeDriver.ts:240), and the ref is set only after a successful pass (ProviderRegistry.ts:666). The break is a manifest edit that keeps the same updatedAt: the new content is accepted but never probed.
verdicts.consequence: After a manifest edit that does not bump updatedAt, the picker shows the old model set until some other probe runs (the per-instance interval or a settings change). The delay is bounded but can be long.
verdicts.scenario: 1) A remote manifest edit adds a model but leaves updatedAt equal to the cached value. 2) refreshOnDemand fetches it: ModelManifest.ts:253 rejects only strictly older manifests, so the fetched copy replaces the cached one at line 257. 3) refreshModelCatalog gets updatedAt equal to probedManifestUpdatedAt (ProviderRegistry.ts:1090) and returns with no probe. 4) The picker shows the old models until a periodic probe runs. The docs say to bump updatedAt when the file changes (model-manifest.md:9-11), but nothing in the checkout enforces it (no match in scripts/ or .github/).

verdicts.summary: Failure amplification (added hazard). If any instance's probe fails, the pass fails and the ref is not advanced, so every picker open runs a full pass over all providers. The fail-fast forEach may also cancel healthy siblings before their syncProvider runs. The mechanism is in the code, but I cannot confirm that a probe fails in practice.
verdicts.consequence: Each picker open would spawn probes for every provider. If the probe is cancelled, healthy providers may never publish their new models from picker-triggered passes. The repeat-per-open cost is new with this commit; the failure path itself predates it for refresh().
verdicts.scenario: 1) One instance's refresh dies: managedProvider.ts:375 wraps refresh in orDie, and checkProvider is typed to fail with ServerSettingsError (managedProvider.ts:46). 2) refreshOneSource (ProviderRegistry.ts:611-626) returns the failure through yield* probe, so the forEach at 660 fails. 3) The owner's Deferred fails, the Ref.set at 666 is skipped, and the loop in refreshModelCatalog (1089-1091) is aborted. 4) The next picker open sees the mismatch again and reruns the full pass.
verdicts.missing: Whether any production path makes refresh() die or fail with a typed error. That needs the error channel of snapshotSettings' getSettings (packages/provider-core/src/server/snapshotSettings, not read) and the driver checkProvider paths. Whether Effect's concurrent forEach interrupts siblings on failure cannot be checked here: the checkout has no node_modules.

verdicts.summary: Boot seed race (added hazard). The ref is seeded from manifestService.current at ProviderRegistry.ts:428, which is not a full pass. Boot probes fork a manifest fetch and read the catalog concurrently at probe start, so they can classify with the disk manifest. If the fetch lands before line 428, the ref records the new updatedAt while providers still reflect the old manifest, and the picker never re-probes.
verdicts.consequence: After a restart, the model picker keeps the models classified from the disk manifest. It shows no refresh until a periodic or settings-driven probe runs.
verdicts.scenario: 1) On boot the disk manifest is older than 1h, so the forced probe's refreshInBackground (CodexDriver.ts:234) starts a network fetch. 2) The probe reads currentCatalog at probe start (CodexDriver.ts:236-238) and gets the disk manifest. 3) The fetch completes and sets manifest to the newer copy before the registry reaches line 428. 4) probedManifestUpdatedAt is seeded with the new updatedAt (line 634), and the next picker open sees a match and does not probe.
verdicts.missing: The relative timing of the background fetch (network) and the layer's construction up to line 428. This is not determinable from source; it needs a runtime trace of the boot sequence.
